([[Jacksonville, Florida]]) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2016–2020) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2020 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2020]]) * NCAA All-time field goal percentage leader (79.4%) * [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2020) * [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] (2020) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2020) * Third-team All-Big 12 (2018) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2016) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] 2016 }} '''Udoka Timothy Azubuike''' ({{IPAc-en|j|uː|ˈ|d|oʊ|k|ə|_|ˌ|æ|z|ə|ˈ|b|uː|k|i}}; born 17 September 1999) is a Nigerian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. ==Early life== Udoka Azubuike was the youngest of five, with two older brothers and two older sisters.{{Cite news |url=https://nypost.com/2018/03/29/kansas-star-will-get-amazing-final-four-moment-seeing-mom/ |title=Kansas star will get amazing Final Four moment: Seeing Mom |last=Kussoy |first=Howard |date=March 29, 2018 |work=[[New York Post]]}} His father, Fabian, was a police officer, and his mother, Florence, was a middle school teacher. Azubuike lost his father to an undiagnosed disease at the age of 10.{{Cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} Nigerian-born, he caught the attention of recruiters with [[Basketball Without Borders]] and was offered a scholarship to play basketball in the United States despite not playing the game until he was 13.{{Cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} He is not related to [[Kelenna Azubuike]], who played parts of four seasons for the [[Golden State Warriors]] and is currently the color analyst for their television broadcasts. ==High school career== Azubuike attended Potter's House Christian Academy in [[Jacksonville, Florida]]. His then assistant coach Harry Coxsome and his wife Donna took care of him and soon became his [[legal guardians]].{{Cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} In his first high school game he was matched up against fellow future Kansas Jayhawk [[Joel Embiid]].{{Cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} Azubuike was a four-year starter averaging 16.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 9.7 [[Rebounds per game|rebounds]] per game his senior year.[http://www.jacksonville.com/sports/high-schools/2016-01-28/story/potters-house-hoops-star-udoka-azubuike-commits-kansas Potter’s House hoops star Udoka Azubuike commits to Kansas] Azubuike was selected to play in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]],[http://www.kansan.com/sports/josh-jackson-and-udoka-azubuike-impress-at-mcdonald-s-all/article_4e5be55e-f6e8-11e5-a609-eb13c6b0d611.html Josh Jackson and Udoka Azubuike impress at McDonald's All-American Game] [[Jordan Brand Classic]],[http://usatodayhss.com/2016/udoka-azubuike-honored-at-first-stop-of-the-jordan-brand-classic-senior-night-tour Udoka Azubuike honored at first stop of the Jordan Brand Classic Senior Night Tour] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].[http://usatodayhss.com/2016/kansas-commit-udoka-azubuike-added-to-world-select-team-at-nike-hoops-summit Kansas commit Udoka Azubuike added to World Select Team at Nike Hoop Summit] He was also a member of the [[National Honor Society]].{{Cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767373-think-reaching-the-final-4-is-tough-then-you-havent-met-kansas-udoka-azubuike |title=Think Reaching the Final 4 Is Tough? Then You Haven't Met Kansas' Udoka Azubuike |last=King |first=Jason |date=March 30, 2018 |work=Bleacher Report}} He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a five-star recruit and was ranked as the 27th best overall player[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article57143928.html Five-star basketball recruit Udoka Azubuike picks Kansas] while [[ESPN]] ranked him 22nd overall in the Class of 2016.[http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/176113/udoka-azubuike ESPN] Azubuike received offers from many universities including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and shortened his final list of colleges to [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], Kansas, and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].[http://www.jacksonville.com/sports/high-schools/2016-01-28/story/potters-house-hoops-star-udoka-azubuike-commits-kansas Potter’s House hoops star Udoka Azubuike commits to Kansas] On 28 January 2016, he announced his choice to play college basketball at the [[University of Kansas]].[https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/01/28/udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks-recruiting-commits Four-star center Udoka Azubuike commits to Kansas] ==College career== ===Freshman year=== In his freshman season he started in six of the 11 games he played in before tearing [[ligament]]s in his left wrist, which ended his season.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/dec/21/ku-freshman-udoka-azubuike-out-season-wrist-injury/ KU freshman Udoka Azubuike out for the season with wrist injury] Before the injury, he averaged 5.0 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.6 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]], and 62.9% [[field goal percentage]]. ===Sophomore year=== For the [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2017–2018 season]], Kansas' coach [[Bill Self]] recruited [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas football]] player James Sosinski to defend Azubuike during practice.{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article207362374.html |title='Pushing and shoving' Doke is this KU walk-on's job. He has bruises to prove it |last=Reiss |first=Aaron |date=March 29, 2018 |work=[[Kansas City Star]]}} Udoka started every game of the regular season but missed the Big 12 tournament after spraining his left [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article203968534.html |title=Udoka Azubuike out for Big 12 Tournament, KU hopeful he can return for NCAAs |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=March 7, 2018 |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 5, 2018}} He returned for the NCAA tournament until KU's loss to eventual champion [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|Final Four]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22957968/mom-see-udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks-play-first |title=Nigeria approves Udoka Azubuike's mother's visa to travel to USA |last=Adelson |first=Andrea |date=March 30, 2018 |work=ESPN |access-date=April 5, 2018}} He averaged 13.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.7 blocks, and led the nation with a 77% field goal percentage for the season.{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/udoka-azubuike-1.html |title=Udoka Azubuike |website=Sports-Reference.com}} His field goal percentage broke the single-season record for Kansas and the [[Big 12 Conference]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article207122189.html |title=A former KU center analyzes the game of Jayhawks big man Udoka Azubuike |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=March 29, 2018 |work=Kansas City Star}} This high percentage was in part due to the majority of his field goals being [[slam dunks]], which typically have a higher completion percentage than jump shots or layups. He had more dunks than any other college player going back to the 2009–2010 season.{{Cite news |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article209693674.html |title=This decade, no player has done what KU's Udoka Azubuike just did |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=April 24, 2018 |work=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 24, 2018}} He was awarded All-Big 12 third team by the conference's coaches{{Cite web |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article203429049.html |title=Devonté Graham, Bill Self take home coaches' All-Big 12 basketball awards |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=March 4, 2018 |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 5, 2018}} and second team by the [[Associated Press|AP]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article203722914.html |title=Devonté Graham, Bill Self win AP All-Big 12 awards |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=March 6, 2018 |website=Kansas City Star |access-date=April 5, 2018}} On 20 April 2018, Azubuike announced his intention to the [[2018 NBA Draft]]. He did not initially hire an agent, which would allow him to return before the combine.{{cite web|title=Kansas' Udoka Azubuike entering draft without agent|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23261307/udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks-declares-nba-draft-hire-agent|website=ESPN.com}} Azubuike was one of a record-high 69 prospects invited to the [[NBA Draft Combine]] that year. On May 17, he measured out to be a near 7' tall center (with shoes on) weighing in at 274 pounds and holding the second-longest wingspan at 7'7", behind only [[Mohamed Bamba]].http://stats.nba.com/draft/combine-anthro/#!?sort=WINGSPAN&dir=1 On 30 May 2018, he announced his intent to withdraw from the draft and return to Kansas for his junior season.{{cite web |title=Udoka Azubuike withdraws from NBA Draft. Here's what his return means for KU |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article212176139.html |website=KansasCity.com}} ===Junior year=== Azubuike was selected as an honorable mention to the 2018–2019 All-Big 12 preseason team.{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article220155170.html#storylink=cpy |title=K-State, KU well represented on All-Big team |last=Newell |first=Jesse |date=Oct 17, 2018 |work=Kansas City Star}} On 4 December 2018, he severely sprained his right ankle against [[2018–19 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team|Wofford]] and missed the following four games.{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article223640115.html#storylink=cpy |title=Azubuike now ’60, 70 percent’ |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=Dec 27, 2018 |work=Kansas City Star}} On 5 January 2019, Azubuike injured his wrist during practice.{{cite web |title=Jayhawks sit out Udoka Azubuike due to wrist injury |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25692183/udoka-azubuike-kansas-jayhawks |website=ESPN.com}} An [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] revealed he tore a ligament in his right hand.{{Cite magazine |last=West |first=Jenna |date=Jan 6, 2019 |title=Kansas' Udoka Azubuike to Undergo Season-Ending Surgery on Right Hand |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/01/06/udoka-azubuike-hand-injury-surgery-season-over-kansas |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} He underwent season-ending surgery on January 9, 2019.{{Cite web |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2019/jan/09/doc-says-azubuikes-surgery-couldnt-have-gone-any-b/ |title=Self: Doc says Azubuike’s surgery ‘couldn’t have gone any better’ |last=Tait |first=Matt |date=Jan 9, 2019 |website=KU Sports.com}} Kansas won all nine games Azubuike played including against top ten teams [[2018–19 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] and [[2018–19 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. He finished the season averaging 13.4 points and 6.8 rebounds.{{Cite news |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article224037655.html |title=KU Coach Bill Self Laments Loss of Azubuike |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=Jan 7, 2019 |work=Kansas City Star}} On 22 April 2019, Azubuike announced he would return to Kansas for his senior season.{{cite web |title=Udoka Azubuike to return for senior season |url=https://kuathletics.com/news/2019/4/22/mens-basketball-udoka-azubuike-to-return-for-senior-season.aspx |website=KUAthletics.com}} According to KU coach Bill Self, “We’re all very excited about Udoka making the decision not to enter the [NBA] draft.” "Unfortunately for him, injury is the reason as he still cannot participate (at) what would be the NBA combine or workouts for the NBA teams."[https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article229530524.html 7-foot center Udoka Azubuike returning to KU for senior season], ''[[Wichita Eagle]]'', Gary Bedore, April 22, 2019. Retrieved April 23, 2019. ===Senior year=== Azubuike scored a career-high 29 points in a 90–84 overtime win over [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] on 27 November 2019.{{cite news |title=No. 4 Kansas beats Dayton 90-84 in overtime for Maui title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401182629 |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 27, 2019}} On 22 February 2020, Azubuike scored 23 points and had a career-high 19 rebounds in a 64–61 win over top-ranked [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]].{{cite news |title=Kansas snaps Baylor's Big 12-record win streak |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28758508/kansas-snaps-baylor-big-12-record-win-streak |accessdate=February 22, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 22, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Azubuike was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]].{{cite press release|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx|title=Men’s Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|date=March 8, 2020 |accessdate=March 8, 2020}} Azubuike averaged 13.7 points, 10.5 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks per game as a senior.{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |accessdate=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} Azubuike's career field goal percentage of 74.9% is the highest in NCAA history. https://kuathletics.com/%f0%9f%94%a5-dok-all-time-ncaa-leader-in-field-goal-percentage/ ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} {|
